Using remote = TRUE (thus incoming = TRUE) run additional checks used CRAN new package submissions. checks identify problems linked URLs (.e., URLs comments). URLs: accessible (e.g., point public GitHub repositories, private repositories) direct links, redirects use protocol http:// instead https:// https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=<pkg> packages https://CRAN.R-project.org/manuals.html refer manuals general URLs form https://CRAN.R-project.org/doc/manuals/r-release/R-exts.html refer specific manual https://CRAN.R-project.org/web/packages/policies.html refer CRAN policies. checks also flag dependencies GitHub, leading NOTEs likeStrong dependencies CRAN BioC software repositories: <pkg>,Suggests Enhances mainstream repositories: <pkg>, andUnknown, possibly misspelled, fields DESCRIPTION: 'Remotes'. intend submit CRAN, can ignore NOTEs. Using TRUE environment variable _R_CHECK_SUGGESTS_ONLY_ run code using dependencies listed Depends, Imports Suggests fields DESCRIPTION file. get warning: Warning get_engine(options$engine): Unknown language engine '<name>' (must registered via knit_engines$set()), probably forgot indicate knit-engine naming code chunk: erroneously tries use engine use-sum, whereas probably intended {r use-sum} correctly indicates r engine used code chunk named use-sum: See sort(names(knitr::knit_engines$get())) available knit-engines. get error Failed error: 'package called '<pkg>'' Quitting <filename>.Rmd:<line numbers> [<chunk name>], probably forgot use library(<pkg>) code chunck, used package declared dependency DESCRIPTION file, used package declared suggested dependency (.e., Suggests field DESCRIPTION file) without running code conditionally presence <pkg> (requireNamespace(<pkg>)) {<code>}. latter catched using argument env_vars = c("_R_CHECK_DEPENDS_ONLY_" = TRUE) running devtools::check(). checks fail LaTeX errors building manual, can use manual = FALSE.

text: Runs checks checks various packages. use pkgcheck::pkgcheck() ‘’ checks largely covered checks devtools used , checks goodpractice already covered , checks pkgstats interesting require system libraries ctags-universal GNU global. However, pkgcheck GitHub action (see also ) might useful.
code: # Select checks # Show groups of checks: goodpractice::all_check_groups() # Show all checks in some groups: goodpractice::checks_by_group(c("cyclocomp", "lintr")) # Run all check from some groups: # goodpractice::goodpractice(checks = goodpractice::checks_by_group(c("cyclocomp", "lintr"))) goodpractice_all_checks <- goodpractice::all_checks() my_checks_goodpractice <- progutils::not_in(   goodpractice_all_checks,   c("covr", # time-consuming and wants 100% coverage     "complexity_function_length", "cyclocomp", # I write complex functions     # The lintr issue `Use == instead of %in% for scalar comparison` should be     # ignored for 'x %in% y' if 'x' or 'y' might contain 'NA' that should be     # removed: 'x %in% NA' and 'NA %in% y' return 'FALSE', whereas 'x == NA' and     # 'NA == y' return 'NA'.     "lintr_scalar_in_linter",     "lintr_line_length_linter",     "lintr_outer_negation_linter", # changes handling of NAs     # flags data.frame() even if 'strings_as_factors' is not explicitly set     "lintr_strings_as_factors_linter",     "tidyverse_brace_linter",     "tidyverse_function_left_parentheses_linter",     "tidyverse_indentation_linter",     "tidyverse_line_length_linter",     "tidyverse_object_name_linter",     "tidyverse_spaces_left_parentheses_linter",     # does not find test-files in inst/tinytest, use check_test_files() instead.     "tidyverse_test_file_names",     "tidyverse_whitespace_linter",          # Checks similar to those from 'rcmdcheck' and 'urlchecker' are also used by     # devtools::check() that already has been run above     goodpractice_all_checks[       grepl(pattern = "^rcmdcheck_|^urlchecker_", x = goodpractice_all_checks)]   ) )  res_goodpractice <- goodpractice::goodpractice(   path = ".", checks = my_checks_goodpractice) res_goodpractice_failed <- goodpractice::failed_checks(res_goodpractice) res_goodpractice_failed  # Can also show output of selected checks through # res_goodpractice$checks$<check_name> res_goodpractice
